source: Direct user messages: initial 1: B; 2: B; 3: A, followed by clarification that all pairs were hard to distinguish and terminology in all texts felt unlike terms people use. Agent UI test clicks excluded.

limitations: Post-hoc case selection; one reader, three pairs, one response per pair.
Version labels hidden on the sheet; no repeated order reversal or independent population sample.
No comprehension accuracy or reading time collected. Qualitative terminology criticism covers all texts; no individual terms identified by the reader.
Does not evaluate 0.3.0, 0.3.1 or 0.3.2; does not establish general superiority or inferiority.
decision: Withdraw the one-versus-two preference interpretation. Record lack of perceptible improvement and dissatisfaction with terminology across both arms. Inspect concrete prose and test familiar explanations of technical concepts; avoid arbitrary synonym replacement or new superiority claims.
initial_counts_status: Superseded as evidence of clear preference by the same respondent clarification; retained only as the original label decoding.

current_interpretation.all_presented_texts_terminology: Reader reported that terms did not feel like those people use.
